questions.question: Choose the correct indefinite article: 'He is ______ honorable judge admired by the entire community.'
questions.explanation: Although 'honorable' begins with the consonant letter 'h', the 'h' is silent and the word starts with a vowel sound (/ˈɒn.ər.ə.bəl/), requiring 'an'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Her elder sister studies at ______ university in Dhaka.'
questions.explanation: 'University' begins with a vowel letter 'u' that produces a consonant glide sound /juː/ (like 'you'), taking 'a' rather than 'an'.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the indefinite article with the word 'one'?

options.label: A
options.text: I saw a one-eyed sailor standing at the harbor.

options.label: B
options.text: I saw an one-eyed sailor standing at the harbor.

options.label: C
options.text: I saw the one-eyed sailor standing at an harbor.

options.label: D
options.text: I saw one-eyed sailor standing at harbor.

questions.correct_answer_text: I saw a one-eyed sailor standing at the harbor.
questions.explanation: 'One' begins with the consonant semivowel sound /w/ ('won'), so it takes the indefinite article 'a'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'He arrived ______ hour earlier than expected.'
questions.explanation: In 'hour', the initial 'h' is silent and the phonetic sound begins with vowel /aʊər/, requiring 'an'.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: 'The prince was declared ______ heir to the imperial throne.'
questions.explanation: 'Heir' has a silent 'h' and sounds like 'air' (/eər/), taking 'an'.

questions.question: Which of the following geographical names MUST take the definite article 'the'?
questions.explanation: Mountain ranges (chains) take 'the' (The Himalayas, The Alps), whereas individual isolated peaks (Mount Everest) do not.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: '______ Padma is one of the most majestic rivers in Bangladesh.'
questions.explanation: Names of rivers, seas, and oceans (The Padma, The Meghna, The Bay of Bengal) always require the definite article 'The'.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'She plays ______ piano with extraordinary elegance.'
questions.explanation: When referring to playing musical instruments as an art or skill, the definite article 'the' is used before the instrument (play the piano/violin/flute).

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The more you practice, ______ better you perform.'
questions.explanation: In parallel proportional comparative structures ('The more... the more...'), 'the' is placed before both comparative adjectives/adverbs.

questions.question: Why is 'the' used in: 'The brave deserve our highest admiration'?

options.label: A
options.text: Because 'the + adjective' functions as a plural collective noun representing a whole class of people

options.label: C
options.text: Because it is followed by a verb

questions.correct_answer_text: Because 'the + adjective' functions as a plural collective noun representing a whole class of people
questions.explanation: 'The + adjective' (the brave, the poor, the rich) designates an entire group of people as a plural collective noun.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: '______ gold is a precious metal.'
questions.explanation: Material and abstract nouns used in a general, unconditional sense take no article (e.g., 'Gold is precious', 'Honesty is the best policy').

questions.question: When does a material noun take the definite article 'the'?

options.label: A
options.text: When it refers to a specific, localized quantity (e.g., 'The gold of this ring is pure')

options.label: C
options.text: Only when the price of gold rises

questions.correct_answer_text: When it refers to a specific, localized quantity (e.g., 'The gold of this ring is pure')
questions.explanation: When an uncountable or material noun is particularized or qualified by an adjectival phrase/clause, it requires 'the'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'They play ______ cricket every Friday afternoon.'
questions.explanation: Names of sports, games, and athletic activities (cricket, football, chess) take no article.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'We had ______ delicious dinner at their home last night.'
questions.explanation: While names of meals generally take no article ('We had dinner'), when preceded by an adjective ('delicious dinner'), they take 'a/an'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'He can speak ______ French fluently, but he does not know ______ French language history.'
questions.explanation: Names of languages alone take no article ('French'), but when accompanied by the word 'language' ('the French language'), 'the' is required.

questions.question: What is the distinction between 'few' and 'a few'?

options.label: A
options.text: 'Few' has a negative meaning (almost none), while 'a few' has a positive meaning (some / a small number)

options.label: B
options.text: 'Few' is used for liquids, 'a few' is used for solids

options.label: D
options.text: There is no difference in meaning

questions.correct_answer_text: 'Few' has a negative meaning (almost none), while 'a few' has a positive meaning (some / a small number)
questions.explanation: 'Few' implies scarcity or insufficiency ('almost none'), while 'a few' denotes a positive, modest quantity ('some').

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'There is ______ milk left in the bottle, hardly enough to make one cup of tea.'
questions.explanation: For uncountable nouns (milk), 'little' has a negative sense (almost none), matching the context 'hardly enough'.

questions.question: Which quantifier is used exclusively with plural countable nouns?
questions.explanation: 'Many' modifies plural countable nouns (books, students), whereas 'much' modifies singular uncountable nouns (water, time).

questions.question: '______ of the two brothers was willing to concede the argument.'
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is used when choosing between exactly two persons or things, taking a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence regarding 'each' and 'every':

options.label: A
options.text: Each student in the seminar was given an individual research project.

options.label: B
options.text: Each student in the seminar were given an individual research project.

options.label: C
options.text: Every of the students received an award.

options.label: D
options.text: Each of students have finished their tasks.

questions.correct_answer_text: Each student in the seminar was given an individual research project.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is distributive, modifying singular nouns and taking singular verbs ('was given'). 'Every of' is ungrammatical.

questions.question: Choose the correct prepositions: 'The seminar begins ______ 9:00 AM ______ Monday morning.'
questions.explanation: Precise clock times take 'at' ('at 9:00 AM'), while days of the week take 'on' ('on Monday morning').

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Bangladesh became independent ______ 1971 ______ December.'
questions.explanation: Years (1971) and months (December) both take the preposition 'in'.

questions.question: What is the distinction between 'between' and 'among'?

options.label: A
options.text: 'Between' is typically used for two distinct entities, while 'among' is used for three or more entities

options.label: B
options.text: 'Between' is for liquids, 'among' is for solids

options.label: C
options.text: 'Among' is only used for inanimate objects

options.label: D
options.text: They are completely interchangeable in all contexts

questions.correct_answer_text: 'Between' is typically used for two distinct entities, while 'among' is used for three or more entities
questions.explanation: 'Between' divides things between two persons/objects, while 'among' distributes among three or more members of a group.

questions.question: 'He has been suffering from fever ______ last Wednesday.'
questions.explanation: In perfect tenses, 'since' marks a specific point in past time ('since last Wednesday'), whereas 'for' marks a duration of time.

questions.question: Choose the correct prepositions: 'He lives ______ Mirpur ______ Dhaka.'
questions.explanation: For smaller localities within a larger city, 'at' is used for the smaller area (Mirpur) and 'in' for the larger city (Dhaka).

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Every conscientious citizen must abide ______ the laws of the land.'
questions.explanation: The idiom 'abide by' means to accept and follow a rule, decision, or law faithfully.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'The patient finally succumbed ______ his prolonged injuries.'
questions.explanation: 'Succumb to' is an appropriate preposition meaning to fail to resist or to die from an illness/injury.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'A genuine scholar is never boastful ______ his intellectual accomplishments.'
questions.explanation: The appropriate adjective preposition pair is 'boastful of' (or 'boast of').

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'He agreed ______ my proposal after reviewing the budget.'
questions.explanation: One 'agrees with' a person, but 'agrees to' a proposal, suggestion, or terms.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'The detective was suspicious ______ the suspect's inconsistent alibi.'
questions.explanation: The standard appropriate preposition is 'suspicious of' (having doubts or mistrust).

topics.topic_name: Prepositions of Motion, Direction and Position

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'The frightened boy jumped ______ the river to escape the fire.'
questions.explanation: 'Into' expresses motion from the outside to the inside of an enclosure or body of water, while 'in' expresses static position.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The hikers walked ______ the dense forest along a narrow winding trail.'
questions.explanation: 'Through' describes movement within a three-dimensional space with boundaries, like a forest, tunnel, or crowd.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'The athlete easily jumped ______ the high wooden hurdle.'
questions.explanation: 'Over' describes motion passing above something from one side to the other without physical contact.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'They strolled peacefully ______ the sandy shore of the Bay of Bengal.'
questions.explanation: 'Along' indicates movement in a line parallel to or following the course of a border, river, road, or shore.

questions.question: 'The cat sprang ______ the table and knocked over the glass vase.'
questions.explanation: 'Onto' signifies movement directed to a position on a surface.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the prepositional idiom 'in spite of'?

options.label: A
options.text: Regardless of or despite the mentioned circumstance

questions.correct_answer_text: Regardless of or despite the mentioned circumstance
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' is synonymous with 'despite', introducing a contrasting obstacle that did not prevent an outcome.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'He succeeded in life ______ hard labor and perseverance.'
questions.explanation: The idiom 'by dint of' means by means of or as a result of (e.g. by dint of hard work).

questions.question: 'We are looking forward to ______ you at the annual convocation.'
questions.explanation: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition (not part of an infinitive), so it must be followed by a gerund (-ing form).

questions.question: What does the prepositional phrase 'in lieu of' mean?

options.label: A
options.text: Instead of or in place of

questions.correct_answer_text: Instead of or in place of
questions.explanation: 'In lieu of' is an idiom derived from French meaning 'in place of' or 'as an alternative to'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'He went to London with an eye to ______ his doctoral research.'
questions.explanation: Phrases ending in prepositions like 'with an eye to' and 'with a view to' take a gerund (verb+ing).

topics.topic_name: Error Detection in Articles and Prepositions

questions.question: Identify the incorrect part: 'He is [A] an European [B] who works as [C] a professor at [D] a university.'
questions.explanation: 'European' begins with the consonant semivowel sound /j/ (yoo-ro-pee-an); the correct article is 'a European', not 'an European'.

questions.question: Spot the error: 'The train arrived [A] at the platform [B] in time [C] on yesterday [D].'
questions.explanation: Temporal adverbs like 'yesterday', 'today', 'tomorrow', 'last week', and 'next year' never take prepositions like 'on' or 'in'.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect usage: 'She died [A] from cancer [B] after battling [C] the illness for [D] months.'
questions.explanation: When someone dies of a specific disease, the correct preposition is 'of' ('died of cancer', not 'died from cancer'). 'Died from' is used for wounds, overwork, etc.

questions.question: Identify the error: 'The man was accused [A] with theft [B] and produced [C] before the magistrate [D].'
questions.explanation: The appropriate preposition after 'accuse' is 'of' ('accused of theft'). One is 'charged with', but 'accused of'.

questions.question: Spot the grammatical flaw: 'He resembles [A] to his father [B] in both appearance [C] and temperament [D].'
questions.explanation: 'Resemble' is a transitive verb that takes a direct object without any preposition (i.e., 'He resembles his father', not 'resembles to').

questions.question: Fill the gaps: 'Education is (a)______ process of acquiring knowledge and developing (b)______ character.'
questions.explanation: 'The process' specifies the defined action, while 'character' is used as an abstract uncountable noun taking no article.

questions.question: Fill the gap: 'Honesty is indispensable (a)______ genuine peace of mind.'
questions.explanation: The appropriate preposition following 'indispensable' is 'to' (or 'for', but 'indispensable to' is preferred in formal board exams).

questions.question: Fill the gap: 'We must abstain (a)______ committing acts that harm (b)______ environment.'
questions.explanation: 'Abstain' takes the preposition 'from' ('abstain from doing something'), and 'the environment' takes the definite article.

questions.question: 'The teacher congratulated the boy (a)______ his brilliant success in (b)______ examination.'
questions.explanation: One 'congratulates someone on' an achievement, and 'the examination' refers to the specific test.

questions.question: 'Blind (a)______ one's own faults makes one incapable (b)______ moral self-correction.'
questions.explanation: 'Blind to' means unwilling to perceive faults, and 'incapable of' is the standard appropriate preposition combination.
